frequency_question: How often do major, highly contested federal economic regulations successfully reach final rule publication in the Federal Register within a 12-month window despite structural administrative friction?
membership_rule: Includes rules classified as economically significant ($100M+ economic impact) that faced high-salience legal or procedural contestation during the rulemaking process. Excludes routine administrative updates.

cases.name: EPA Clean Power Plan Repeal / Affordable Clean Energy Rule
OSHA COVID-19 Vaccination and Testing ETS

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named prominent contested rules; all successfully published final versions within their administrative windows despite substantial structural and legal friction.
known_gaps: Sample focuses on rules that successfully reached final publication; does not comprehensively capture rules abandoned pre-proposal due to internal friction.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 finalized rules in the designated sample of heavily contested major regulations that successfully reached the Federal Register within the target timeframe.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to standard Administrative Procedure Act (APA) structural constraints which remain stable across presidential terms.
